newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli food venture stake to be offered Unilever.
newsitem.headline: Israeli food venture stake to be offered Unilever.

text.p: Unilever PLC will be invited to join a projected Israeli joint venture for marketing and distributing frozen food, a source involved in the talks to form the new company said on Wednesday.
The joint venture is now under negotiation between Sunfrost Ltd and Strauss Dairies, Clal Industries, Sunfrost's parent, said in an announcment to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
The announcement did not provide any further details, but the source said the two sides planned to give Unilever PLC an option to take a stake in the projected joint venture after it was formed.
The source said the option was contingent on Unilever giving the joint venture exclusive rights to distribute Unilever frozen food products in Israel.
A Unilever official said that at this stage the company was not involved in the talks.
Unilever acquired a 50 percent interest in Strauss' ice cream business in September 1995 and has been making other acquisitions in Israel mainly in chemicals and personal care products.
The source said Sunfrost and Strauss would hold the joint venture in equal shares unless or until Unilever joined.
"In the first stage, all the distribution operations of Sunfrost will be transferred to the joint venture. In the second stage there will be new and imported products," the source said.
He said Strauss, Israel's largest privately controlled dairy, would not be distributing its ice cream through the joint venture at this stage.

Sunfrost, which is 57 percent-controlled by Clal industries, produces and distributes a wide range of frozen foods. The company has not been profitable for some time, and in the first nine months of 1996 it lost 43.9 million shekels ($13 million) on sales of 106.2 million shekels.
Clal had been seeking to sell Sunfrost and reportedly held talks with Unilever and the Pillsbury Co.
